This Book guides those conscious of Allah, who believe in the unseen, pray, spend and are certain of the Hereafter, while Allah has sealed the hearts of those who disbelieve.
Allah gives even the example of a mosquito; believers know it is the truth, disbelievers question it, and by it He guides many and misleads the defiantly disobedient.
Those given the Book who recite it as it should be recited believe in it, and whoever disbelieves in it is among the losers.
Worldly life is made attractive to disbelievers who ridicule the believers, and those given the Scripture differed out of envy while Allah guided the believers to the truth.
Believers who do righteous deeds are promised forgiveness and great reward, while those who disbelieve and deny Allah's signs are companions of Hellfire.
One who was dead and given life and light to walk among people is not like one in darkness who never emerges.
When messengers bring the children of Adam Allah's verses, those who fear Him and reform have no fear or grief, while those who deny them arrogantly abide in the Fire.
The bedouins are stronger in disbelief and hypocrisy; some count their spending a loss, while others believe and count it a means of nearness to Allah.
Those who believe, do righteous deeds and humble themselves to their Lord abide in Paradise; the two parties are like the blind and deaf against the seeing and hearing.
Those who respond to their Lord, keep His covenant, are patient, pray and spend enter gardens greeted by angels; covenant-breakers who spread corruption get the curse and Hell.
Disbelievers boast to believers of their better standing, though richer generations were destroyed; they will learn who is worst, while Allah increases the guided in guidance.
The Prophet is only a clear warner: believers who do righteous deeds receive forgiveness and noble provision, while those who strive against Allah's verses are companions of Hellfire.
Turn to the correct religion before an unavoidable Day when people divide: disbelievers bear their disbelief, and believers who do righteousness are rewarded from Allah's bounty.
Whoever submits to Allah while doing good holds the most trustworthy handhold, and the Prophet need not grieve over disbelievers, who enjoy a little before a massive punishment.
Believers and the defiantly disobedient are not equal: believers have the Gardens of Refuge, the disobedient the Fire, and a nearer punishment short of the greater, that perhaps they repent.
Disbelievers will have severe punishment, while believers who do righteous deeds will have forgiveness and great reward.
The blind and seeing, darkness and light, shade and heat, living and dead are not equal; Allah makes hear whom He wills, but the Prophet cannot make the buried hear.
Most will not believe, shackled and screened so warning them makes no difference; the warning reaches only one who follows the message and fears the Most Merciful unseen.
Allah did not create the heaven and earth aimlessly, as disbelievers assume, nor will He treat righteous believers like corrupters or the God-fearing like the wicked.
Man calls on his Lord in adversity but, once favored, forgets Him and sets up equals, unlike one praying devoutly at night, fearing the Hereafter and hoping for mercy.
Liars about Allah who deny the truth have a residence in Hell, while those who bring and believe the truth will have whatever they desire with their Lord.
The blind and the seeing are not equal, nor are those who believe and do righteous deeds equal to the evildoer.
Evildoers will not be made equal to righteous believers in life and death; Allah created the heavens and earth in truth so every soul is recompensed without wrong.
Allah wastes the deeds of disbelievers who avert people from His way, and removes the misdeeds of believers who believe in what was sent down upon Muhammad, the truth.
Allah supports believers who support Him; disbelievers who disliked His revelation have misery and wasted deeds and face the fate of those before, for they have no protector.
Disbelievers who avert people from Allah's path and oppose the Messenger cannot harm Him and are not forgiven if they die so; believers must obey Allah and the Messenger.
Believers in Allah and His messengers are the supporters of truth and the martyrs with their Lord, while those who disbelieve and deny His verses are companions of Hellfire.
Allah's examples: the wives of Noah and Lot, who betrayed their husbands and were told to enter the Fire, and the believing wife of Pharaoh and Mary, daughter of 'Imran.
The righteous have Gardens of Pleasure; deniers are asked whether Muslims would be treated like criminals, and what scripture, oath or partners support their claims.
Criminals used to laugh and wink at the believers and call them lost; on that Day the believers, on couches, will laugh at the disbelievers.
Remind, for whoever fears Allah takes heed while the wretched avoid it and burn in the greatest Fire; whoever purifies himself, remembers his Lord's name and prays succeeds.
Such believers are the companions of the right, while those who disbelieve in Allah's signs are the companions of the left, with fire closed over them.
Disbelievers among the People of the Scripture and the polytheists abide in Hell, the worst of creatures, while righteous believers, the best of creatures, abide in gardens, pleased with Allah.
